findings.title: Data Fusion's ip_allocation CIDR is never reserved via Private Service Access peering
findings.explanation: A private Cloud Data Fusion instance's network_config.ip_allocation must be a CIDR range already reserved for the target VPC via a google_compute_global_address (purpose = VPC_PEERING) peered to servicenetworking.googleapis.com through google_service_networking_connection. The example passes ip_allocation = "10.92.48.0/22" against google_compute_network.private, which is a bare custom-mode VPC (auto_create_subnetworks = false) with no subnets, no reserved global address, and no service networking connection anywhere in the repo. Each resource passes its own checks individually (holden has no rule correlating google_data_fusion_instance.network_config.ip_allocation against google_service_networking_connection.reserved_peering_ranges across three resource types), but the composition means instance creation is likely to fail with a 'network does not have a private connection to source services' error from the Data Fusion API, the same class of pre-flight-plumbing gap as the CMEK IAM grant already fixed in this file.
findings.remediation: Add a google_compute_global_address (purpose = VPC_PEERING, address_type = INTERNAL, address = "10.92.48.0", prefix_length = 22, network = google_compute_network.private.id) and a google_service_networking_connection (network = google_compute_network.private.id, service = "servicenetworking.googleapis.com", reserved_peering_ranges = [that address's name]), and add the connection to module.datafusion's depends_on alongside the existing KMS binding.

findings.suppression_reason: Won't fix — user (james.woolfenden@gmail.com) declined a time_sleep-based mitigation as an arbitrary workaround. Accepted as residual risk: Data Fusion instance provisioning takes 20-30+ minutes, so IAM propagation (seconds to a couple minutes) will almost always complete before the control plane needs the CMEK grant. If it ever does fail on first apply, the fix is a plain terraform apply re-run.
findings.title: CMEK IAM grant and the resource that depends on it are ordered by Terraform but not by IAM propagation
findings.explanation: depends_on = [google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.datafusion] guarantees Terraform issues the IAM grant API call before the Data Fusion create call, but Cloud IAM bindings are eventually consistent — the grant can take up to several minutes to propagate. No deterministic rule models this because it's a timing property of the GCP control plane, not a static attribute. In practice Data Fusion instance provisioning itself runs for many minutes, so the window is usually absorbed, but this is not guaranteed and has been a known source of flaky first-apply failures in other Data Fusion CMEK setups.
findings.remediation: If a first-apply failure is ever observed here, add a short time_sleep (time provider) between google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.datafusion and module.datafusion, or document that a re-run of terraform apply resolves it. Not applying a fix now since the right choice (accept vs. add a sleep) is a judgment call, not a mechanical one.
